You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like April 2020. Industrial production, payrolls and the activity index are all at extreme lows, and unemployment is at an extreme high, which fits the COVID shock. Headline and core CPI are very low, and the dollar is strong.

The question is whether it is March or April 2020. VIX has a 3-month change of -1.5 while its level is still +1.5. In March 2020 the VIX peaked at about 80, so its z-score would have been higher. By April it had come down to about 34, which fits a +1.5 level and a falling 3-month change. Unemployment at +3.0 points to April, when it reached 14.7%. Payrolls averaged -3.0 over 3 months, which also fits April. The policy rate z of -2.0 with a 3-month change of 0 suggests the cut to zero was already in the 3-month window or just before it, which fits April, since the cuts came in March.

Equity 1-month return is -3.0, which would fit March, as April 2020 had a big rally. Equity 3-month return of -1.0 and 6-month of -2.5 also fit March better. The Baa spread 3-month change of -1.5 looks odd for March, though, when spreads spiked.

Industrial production at -3.0 with a 3-month change of -3.0 suggests April 2020 (data through March or April). If the data were as of end-March, unemployment would have been only 4.4%, which is a z of about +2 to +3. Mixed signals, but March 2020 fits the markets better.

Treasury 7-10y 1-month return is -1.5, and 20y+ is -1.0, which fits March 2020, when yields rose late in the month and long Treasuries fell. Investment-grade credit 1-month return is -2.0, which also fits March (about -7%). A 3-month IG return of +1.0 is odd, though.

Taken together, I'd go with March 2020 or possibly April.
